hints: Notice the words connected in series and made from the same metal - this tells you current $I$ is the same in X and Y and number density $n$ of free electrons is the same.
Recall $I = nAvq$ for drift speed $v$ and cross-sectional area $A$, so with $I$, $n$ and $q$ fixed, $v$ is inversely proportional to $A$.
Compare the areas from the diameters: $A = \pi d^2/4$, so doubling $d$ for wire Y makes its area four times the area of wire X, then invert for the $v_X/v_Y$ ratio.
walkthrough: Series connection means the same charge per second passes through both wires, so $I_X = I_Y = I$. Same metal means free electron number density $n$ and charge $q$ are the same.
Use $I = nAvq$ rearranged for drift speed: $v = I/(nAq)$. For fixed $I$, $n$ and $q$, $v$ is proportional to $1/A$.
Relate area to diameter with $A = \pi d^2/4$, so $A$ is proportional to $d^2$. Given $d_Y = 2d_X$, then $A_Y/A_X = (2)^2 = 4$.
Substitute $A_Y/A_X = 4$ to get $v_X/v_Y = 4/1$. This is option D.

options.A: This inverts the ratio. The thinner wire X must have the larger drift speed to carry the same series current.
options.B: This uses the diameter ratio of 2 directly. Drift speed depends on cross-sectional area, which depends on $d^2$, not $d$.
options.C: This gives the diameter ratio $2/1$. The area ratio is $4$, so the drift speed ratio is larger than 2.
options.D: Same current and same $n$ give $v$ proportional to $1/A$. Since $A_Y = 4A_X$, then $v_X/v_Y = 4/1$.
